etymologies.etymologyHTML: From scholar +‎ -ship.

quote.citation: 2013, Stuart Wolfendale, Imperial to International, page 192:
quote.text: There were proposals to revive choir scholarships, because a shortage of regular choristers meant that weddings often went choirless.

definitions.definition: The character or qualities of a scholar.
The activity, methods or attainments of a scholar.
(uncountable) The sum of knowledge accrued by scholars; the realm of refined learning.

quote.citation: 2010, Michael T. Cooper, Contemporary Druidry: A Historical and Ethnographic Study, →ISBN:
quote.text: I found the website and found people mingling scholarship with faith – great googly moogly!

definitions.definition: (Australia, dated) The first year of high school, often accompanied by exams that needed to be passed before advancement to the higher grades.
(intransitive) To attend an institution on a scholarship.

quote.citation: 2012, Joseph Miller, The Wicked Wine of Democracy‎[1], →ISBN, page 205:
quote.text: Up from the tenements of the Lower East Side, he had scholarshiped at Cornell and Harvard Law.
In the first year, twenty children were scholarshiped to attend the Kids Across America Kamp in Branson, Missouri.

quote.citation: 2012, Bernard W. Taylor, Introduction to Management Science:‎[3], page 632:
quote.text: Judith Lewis is a doctoral student at State University, and she also works full-time as an academic tutor for 10 scholarshiped student athletes.
